def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction:
## Definition

Work over the real field with standard coordinate inner products. Let
$A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite (equivalently,
positive definite in the Cholesky convention of
[[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]]) and let
$P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank, where $1\le m\le n$.
The map $P$ sends coarse-grid coordinate vectors to fine-grid coordinate
vectors; its Euclidean adjoint is the transpose $P^{\mathsf T}$ by
[[thm-matrix-of-the-adjoint-is-the-conjugate-transpose]]. Define the **Galerkin
coarse matrix**

$$A_H:=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP.$$

Whenever $A_H$ is invertible, define the **exact Galerkin coarse-correction
error map**

$$C:=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h.$$

This definition is conditional on invertibility of $A_H$. The next theorem
proves that condition from positive definiteness of $A_h$ and full column rank
of $P$. The formula is in exact real arithmetic; a rediscretized operator is
not identified with $A_H$ unless equality is separately shown.
lem-zero-boundary-piecewise-affine-funct:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $v:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and affine
on each interval of a finite partition $0=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_N=1$, with
$v(0)=v(1)=0$. Then the Sobolev class of $v$ belongs to
$H^1_0(0,1)=W^{1,2}_0((0,1);\mathbb R)$, where $W^{1,2}_0$ is the norm
closure of $C_c^\infty(0,1)$ in $W^{1,2}(0,1)$.
thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy:
## Statement

Let $A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let
$P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank. Put
$A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$. Then $A_H$ is symmetric positive definite, hence
invertible, and the map $C=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$ of
[[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]] satisfies

$$C^2=C,\qquad CP=0,\qquad P^{\mathsf T}A_hC=0,\qquad C^{\mathsf T}A_h=A_hC.$$

Consequently $\operatorname{Ran}(C)=\operatorname{Ran}(P)^{\perp_{A_h}}$;
$C$ is the orthogonal projector onto that complement in the energy inner
product $\langle x,y\rangle_{A_h}:=x^{\mathsf T}A_hy$.
def-symmetric-two-grid-error-operator:
## Definition

Let $A_h$ be symmetric positive definite, let $C$ be the Galerkin projector
of [[thm-galerkin-coarse-correction-is-energy-orthogonal-projector]], and let
$S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be a linear pre-smoothing error map. For the
energy inner product of [[def-energy-inner-product-and-norm-for-a-hermitian-positive-definite-matrix]],
define the **$A_h$-adjoint** of $S$ by

$$S^{*_{A_h}}:=A_h^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}A_h.$$

This is well-defined because $A_h$ is invertible. For all $x,y$,
$\langle Sx,y\rangle_{A_h}=x^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}A_hy
=\langle x,S^{*_{A_h}}y\rangle_{A_h}$, so it is the adjoint with respect to
that energy inner product. The **symmetric two-grid error map** is

$$E:=S^{*_{A_h}}CS.$$

It maps an input error through pre-smoothing $S$, exact coarse correction $C$,
and the $A_h$-adjoint post-smoother.
alg-aggregation-based-algebraic-multigri:
## Definition

This is a finite aggregation-based algebraic multigrid **setup** procedure; it
constructs a hierarchy and does not claim that any cycle converges. All
arithmetic and comparisons below are exact. An admissible input consists of an
integer $n_0\ge1$, a real symmetric positive-definite matrix
$A_0=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{n_0\times n_0}$ whose off-diagonal
entries satisfy $a_{ij}\le0$, a real threshold $0<\theta<1$, a coarse-size
threshold $n_{\min}\ge1$, and a level cap $L\ge0$. A matrix with these sign
and definiteness conditions is the matrix class used here. The terms
**strength graph**, **aggregate**, **prolongation**, and **Galerkin hierarchy**
are defined by the steps below.

1. Set $\ell=0$, $n_\ell=\dim A_\ell$, and retain $A_\ell$ in the output. If
   $n_\ell\le n_{\min}$, return status `coarse-reached`.
2. If $\ell=L$ before the stop test in step 1 succeeds, return status
   `level-cap`.
3. On vertices $1,\ldots,n_\ell$, place an undirected edge $\{i,j\}$ for
   $i\ne j$ exactly when $a_{ij}^{(\ell)}<0$ and at least one of
   $$-a_{ij}^{(\ell)}\ge\theta\max_{k\ne i}(-a_{ik}^{(\ell)}),\qquad -a_{ij}^{(\ell)}\ge\theta\max_{k\ne j}(-a_{jk}^{(\ell)})$$
   holds. This finite graph is the strength graph at level $\ell$.
4. Let $U=\{1,\ldots,n_\ell\}$ and start with no aggregates. While $U\ne\varnothing$, let $i$ be the smallest element of $U$, create one aggregate
   $$C_r=\{i\}\cup\bigl(N(i)\cap U\bigr),$$
   where $N(i)$ is its strength-graph neighbour set, then remove every element of $C_r$ from $U$. This produces an ordered family of aggregates.
5. Let $n_{\ell+1}$ be the number of aggregates. If $n_{\ell+1}\ge n_\ell$, return status `coarsening-stalled` with the hierarchy through level $\ell$. Otherwise form the indicator prolongation
   $$(P_\ell)_{ir}=1\text{ if }i\in C_r,\qquad (P_\ell)_{ir}=0\text{ otherwise},$$
   form the Galerkin coarse matrix $A_{\ell+1}=P_\ell^{\mathsf T}A_\ell P_\ell$, append $P_\ell,A_{\ell+1}$, replace $\ell$ by $\ell+1$, and return to step 1.

The result contains all completed matrices and prolongations and exactly one
status: `coarse-reached`, `level-cap`, or `coarsening-stalled`. Reaching any
status is not a convergence or quality certificate.
lem-one-dimensional-poisson-smoothing-an:
## Statement

Let $N=2M\ge4$, $h=1/N$, and let $A_h\in\mathbb R^{(N-1)\times(N-1)}$ have diagonal $2/h$, adjacent off-diagonal entries $-1/h$, and all other entries zero. This is the Dirichlet stiffness matrix for the uniform one-dimensional Poisson mesh. Let $P\in\mathbb R^{(N-1)\times(M-1)}$ linearly interpolate from the coarse nodes at even fine indices: set coarse endpoint values $v_0=v_M=0$, $(Pv)_{2j}=v_j$, and $(Pv)_{2j+1}=(v_j+v_{j+1})/2$ wherever these are interior fine indices. Put $A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$, $C=I-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$, and $S=I-A_h/\lambda_{\max}(A_h)$. Then for every integer $\nu\ge1$ and every fine vector $e$,

$$\|CS^\nu e\|_{A_h}^2\le\frac{2}{2\nu+1}\|e\|_{A_h}^2.$$

The separate estimates proved below are the exact approximation bound
$\|Cw\|_{A_h}^2\le(h/2)\|A_hw\|_2^2$ and smoothing bound
$\|A_hS^\nu e\|_2^2\le4\,[h(2\nu+1)]^{-1}\|e\|_{A_h}^2$; their constants are compatible and independent of $N$.
alg-finite-galerkin-v-cycle:
## Definition

Fix a finite Galerkin hierarchy of real SPD matrices
$A_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j\times n_j}$, $0\le j\le J$, with $n_j\ge1$, and
full-column-rank prolongations $P_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j\times n_{j-1}}$
satisfying $A_{j-1}=P_j^{\mathsf T}A_jP_j$ for $1\le j\le J$. Choose
nonnegative integer sweep counts $\nu_1,\nu_2$, a positive integer cycle
count $\gamma$, and matrices $K_j^{\mathrm{pre}},K_j^{\mathrm{post}}\in
\mathbb R^{n_j\times n_j}$ for $1\le j\le J$; $^{\mathsf T}$ denotes the
transpose of [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]. An invocation
$\operatorname{Cycle}(j,x,b)$ takes $x,b\in\mathbb R^{n_j}$ and returns an
approximate solution to $A_jz=b$:

1. If $j=0$, return the exact solution $A_0^{-1}b$.
2. Starting from $x$, perform $\nu_1$ pre-sweeps
   $x\leftarrow x+K_j^{\mathrm{pre}}(b-A_jx)$ and set $r=b-A_jx$.
3. Set $e=0$. For $t=1,\ldots,\gamma$, replace $e$ by the recursive iterate
   $$e\leftarrow\operatorname{Cycle}(j-1,e,P_j^{\mathsf T}r).$$
4. Correct $x\leftarrow x+P_je$, then perform $\nu_2$ post-sweeps
   $x\leftarrow x+K_j^{\mathrm{post}}(b-A_jx)$; return $x$.

The V-cycle is $\gamma=1$ and the W-cycle is $\gamma=2$. Each call decreases
$j$, so the recursion is finite. The definition fixes exact arithmetic; setup
cost, floating-point error, and convergence of the recursive cycle are separate
claims.
thm-two-grid-energy-contraction-under-jo:
## Statement

Let $A_h$, $C$, $S$, and $E=S^{*_{A_h}}CS$ be as in
[[def-symmetric-two-grid-error-operator]]. Suppose $0\le\rho<1$ and

$$\|CSx\|_{A_h}^2\le\rho\|x\|_{A_h}^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.$$

Then $E$ is self-adjoint and nonnegative in the $A_h$ inner product, and its
operator norm induced by $\|\cdot\|_{A_h}$ satisfies $\|E\|_{A_h}\le\rho$.
A rate derived from separate smoothing and approximation inequalities requires
a proof that those inequalities imply this joint estimate.
thm-aggregation-amg-hierarchy-preserves-:
## Statement

For every admissible input to
[[alg-aggregation-based-algebraic-multigrid-hierarchy]], each successful
aggregation partitions the current indices into nonempty disjoint sets. Its
indicator prolongation has full column rank. Every successful Galerkin product
$A_{\ell+1}=P_\ell^{\mathsf T}A_\ell P_\ell$ is symmetric positive definite
with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. The setup procedure terminates after at
most $L$ coarsening attempts and returns exactly one of `coarse-reached`,
`level-cap`, or `coarsening-stalled`. These structural properties do not imply
multigrid convergence.
thm-galerkin-v-cycle-work-recurrence-mas:
## Statement

Suppose each level with $N$ unknowns has $cN$ arithmetic work outside
recursion, its next level has $N/q$ unknowns for a fixed $q=2^d>1$, the base
solve at $N=1$ has bounded positive cost, and each cycle makes $\gamma\ge1$
recursive calls as in [[alg-finite-galerkin-v-cycle]]. For $N=q^L$ the work
recurrence

$$T(N)=cN+\gamma T(N/q)$$

has order $\Theta(N)$ when $\gamma<q$, $\Theta(N\log N)$ when $\gamma=q$,
and $\Theta(N^{\log_q\gamma})$ when $\gamma>q$. These are arithmetic-work
bounds conditional on the stated uniform per-level cost and coarsening
assumptions. They do not imply convergence or include setup cost.
thm-one-dimensional-poisson-two-grid-ene:
## Statement

For the nested one-dimensional Poisson grids and prolongation of
[[lem-one-dimensional-poisson-smoothing-and-approximation]], take the
pre-smoothing error map to be $S^\nu$, with $S=I-A_h/\lambda_{\max}(A_h)$,
and take the post-smoother to be its $A_h$-adjoint. The resulting symmetric
two-grid error map satisfies

$$\|E\|_{A_h}\le\frac{2}{2\nu+1}\le\frac23<1\qquad(\nu\ge1),$$

uniformly for all even $N=2M\ge4$. This proves one concrete level-uniform
two-grid rate; it does not assert convergence of an arbitrary AMG hierarchy.
